principles: A Christian family is not assumed to have a universal sanctoral.
Calendar systems, Paschal computation, jurisdiction and church body are stored explicitly.
The same person may have distinct observance dates, ranks or no liturgical observance in different churches.
Source authority is evaluated per claim type; official does not imply reusable full text.
Names are entity-linked across languages, but display labels are localized independently of source language.

calendarPolicies.sanctoral-normative: Official calendar includes saints/commemorations with normative dates/ranks.
calendarPolicies.commemorative-normative: Official commemorative calendar exists, but terminology/rank differs from a Catholic/Orthodox sanctoral.
calendarPolicies.lectionary-year: Primary normative structure is church year/lectionary rather than a universal saints calendar.
calendarPolicies.emphasis-days: Official days/weeks/sabbaths of emphasis exist; they are institutional observances, not saints.
calendarPolicies.no-universal-sanctoral: No universal normative saints-of-the-day system should be inferred.
calendarPolicies.no-normative-liturgical-calendar: Tradition explicitly does not prioritize a fixed liturgical/holy-day calendar.
calendarPolicies.church-specific: Policy varies by member church/jurisdiction; resolve locally.
calendarPolicies.church-specific-normative: A normative calendar exists at individual church/jurisdiction level.
calendarPolicies.unknown-local: Discover and verify local practice before publication.

families.label: Catholic — Latin Church
families.calendarNotes: General Roman Calendar plus national, diocesan, religious-order and proper calendars; movable feasts calculated separately.

families.label: Catholic — Eastern Churches sui iuris
families.calendarNotes: Each sui iuris Church retains its own liturgical tradition, menologion, calendar reforms and Paschal practice. Never inherit the Latin calendar by default.

families.label: Eastern Orthodox
families.calendarNotes: Sanctoral and movable cycle vary by autocephalous/autonomous Church and by Julian/Revised Julian/Gregorian fixed-date usage and Paschalion.

families.label: Coptic Orthodox
families.calendarNotes: Coptic calendar and Synaxarium; preserve Coptic/Gregorian mapping and local rank/fasting data.

families.label: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo
families.calendarNotes: Ethiopian calendar, Senksar, recurring monthly commemorations and distinct movable-feast computation.

families.label: Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo
families.calendarNotes: Do not assume Ethiopian calendar records are identical; discover Eritrean official sources separately.

families.label: Armenian Apostolic
families.calendarNotes: Official Mother See calendar includes saints, fasts and movable feasts; diaspora jurisdictions may require local variants.

families.label: Syriac Orthodox
families.calendarNotes: Use patriarchal and jurisdictional sources; preserve Syriac/Arabic/English names and liturgical terminology.

families.label: Malankara Orthodox Syrian
families.calendarNotes: Use official Panjangom/calendar and lectionary; preserve Malayalam/local jurisdiction variants.

families.label: Assyrian Church of the East / East Syriac tradition
families.calendarNotes: Use official Church calendar and lectionary; model East Syriac seasons and feasts independently.

families.label: Anglican
families.calendarNotes: Province-specific calendars and authorized commemorations; Church of England and Episcopal Church are not universal proxies for all Anglican provinces.

families.label: Lutheran
families.calendarNotes: Some churches publish saints/commemorations; others emphasize church year and lectionary. Resolve per member church.

families.label: Reformed / Presbyterian / Congregational / United-Uniting
families.calendarNotes: Do not infer a universal sanctoral. Use RCL/church-year resources and any local commemorations explicitly promulgated.

families.label: Methodist / Wesleyan
families.calendarNotes: Church year, RCL and special Sundays are primary; local calendars may differ by denomination.

families.label: Baptist
families.calendarNotes: Use official bodies for church identity, history, prayer/worship resources and special events; never manufacture saints-of-the-day.

families.label: Pentecostal / Assemblies traditions
families.calendarNotes: Official emphasis/event calendars may exist, but they are not sanctorals.

families.label: Seventh-day Adventist
families.calendarNotes: General Conference Special Days and Sabbaths are institutional observances, not a saints calendar.

families.label: Anabaptist / Mennonite / Brethren in Christ
families.calendarNotes: Church-year worship resources may exist; no universal saint calendar should be assumed.

families.label: Moravian / Unitas Fratrum
families.calendarNotes: Lectionary and Daily Texts are central structured resources.

families.label: Religious Society of Friends (Quakers)
families.calendarNotes: Historical Quaker witness treats all times as holy; represent this explicitly rather than creating a feast calendar.

families.label: The Salvation Army
families.calendarNotes: Use territorial structures, leadership, history and official observances; no saint calendar should be inferred.

families.label: Old Catholic / Union of Utrecht
families.calendarNotes: Resolve calendars per member church; do not infer a single universal Union calendar without evidence.

families.label: African Instituted / Free / Independent Churches
families.calendarNotes: Discover practice from the church body's own sources; WCC and national councils are discovery roots only.
